pr_comments: This seems like it may be blocked by https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/93320

Ran into issues due to GRPC update to 1.33.2 in cadvisor from https://github.com/google/cadvisor/pull/2716. We can't update grpc in k/k due breakage with etcd (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/93320#issuecomment-685237947).

Rolled back grpc to 1.27.1 in cadvisor and cut a new release, v0.38.1

We hit another issue due to cadvisor importing a staging repo causing a recursion (circular dependency): https://github.com/google/cadvisor/pull/2726

Thanks @dims for the fix there. I cut another patch release v0.38.2 with the fix. Let's try to vendor again :)
Looking better now, the tests are alot more green!

Thanks @JornShen, we might need to do a cherrypick for that issue if necessary.

Almost there, but one of the the e2e tests is failing `pull-kubernetes-bazel-test`. Specifically, `//test/conformance/conformance_test:run_1_of_2` is failing.

Chatting with @dims offline, failure is due to the vendor update of `gopkg.in/yaml.v2 v2.2.8` to `gopkg.in/yaml.v2 v2.3.0`. Apparently v2.3.0 has a [breaking change](https://github.com/go-yaml/yaml/pull/571) that changed the default max YAML line length from 80 characters to unlimited characters. 

This is an issue for us because [Conformance test](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5e44d8ebafc866e132530fa1328872561ba5f6da/test/conformance/walk.go) generates some YAML config and does a git diff from what is checked into k/k.  Due to this change the conformance tests are failing since there is a diff in the output yaml due to the line length change of this library.  

More discussion about this issue in here as well: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/95571#issuecomment-708796327

Next steps sounds like one of the following options: 

1. Attempt to revert back to v2.2.8 of the library 
   * (need to check if this will be possible or one of the transitive dependencies needs >= v2.3.0)
2. See if we can somehow force the library to use 80 character limit as before
3. Regen the Conformance YAML under v2.3.0 of the library

option#2 doesn't sound possible -- there is a v3 version of the library but that also doesn't support line length (same behavior of unlimited length line as v2.3.0) ref: https://github.com/go-yaml/yaml/pull/455 and https://github.com/go-yaml/yaml/pull/455#issuecomment-624939185

I think the reason that `gopkg.in/yaml.v2` needed to be updated from `v2.2.8` to `v2.3.0` is because https://github.com/google/cadvisor/pull/2716 upgraded `github.com/prometheus/common` from `v0.10.0` to `v0.15.0`. 

As part of that upgrade, looks like `github.com/prometheus/common@v0.15.0` requires `gopkg.in/yaml.v2@v2.3.0` ref: https://github.com/prometheus/common/pull/242. 

An interm solution might be to rollback the upgrade of `github.com/prometheus/common` in cadvisor to ensure k/k can stay on `gopkg.in/yaml.v2@v2.2.8`, but this will be a short term solution...
@bobbypage let's regen the conformance yaml :) was just trying to avoid some extra approvals. We'll ping people needed.

> @bobbypage let's regen the conformance yaml :)

no, the yaml bump would affect all serialized yaml output. see identical discussion in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/95571#issuecomment-709315815

New cadvisor v0.38.3 has been cut with the `gopkg.in/yaml.v2` reverted back to `v2.2.8`. https://github.com/google/cadvisor/pull/2728 

Let's try again... :)

The approach the go.uber.org libraries have taken to expressing their development tool dependencies is really unfortunate, because it passes those development-time dependencies on to their library consumers.

The majority of the newly vendored dependencies are because of the tools.go files in `go.uber.org/{atomic,multierr,zap}`

Setting up a test copy of those modules that deletes that tools.go file and revendoring drops all of the following (roughly 45kloc):

* vendor/github.com/BurntSushi/toml
* vendor/go.uber.org/tools
* vendor/golang.org/x/lint
* vendor/honnef.co/go/tools

I'm not sure what to do with vendor/honnef.co/go/tools/LICENSE-THIRD-PARTY ... our license gathering script doesn't aggregate it, and I'm not sure whether it should or not.

Thanks for looking more closely at the vendored changes. I looked into the increase of deps and it seems it was caused by https://github.com/google/cadvisor/pull/2716 

```
$ git checkout f6f48d031d729c3b38629c63e5c6ebb1a6ca76fc && go list -m all | wc -l
275
```

Before it was at 137 deps

```
$ git checkout f6f48d031d729c3b38629c63e5c6ebb1a6ca76fc^1 && go list -m all | wc -l
Previous HEAD position was f6f48d03 Update dependencies
HEAD is now at bf8fe422 Delete exclude guest flag which causing problems on some configurations. (#2640)
137
```
The reason for the increase deps in https://github.com/google/cadvisor/pull/2716  was probably due to upgrade of GRPC, but we reverted that in https://github.com/google/cadvisor/pull/2724 and also the `gopkg.in/yaml.v2` https://github.com/google/cadvisor/pull/2728. The issue looks like somewhere along the way we forgot to run `go mod tidy` 😮. 

I ran `go mod tidy` and we're back to reasonable amount of deps, 140:

```
$ git checkout v0.38.4 && go list -m all | wc -l
140
```

cadvisor should really add a tidy check to CI, I filed https://github.com/google/cadvisor/issues/2730 for us to do that. 

I cut another cadvisor release after running tidy, https://github.com/google/cadvisor/pull/2731, cadvisor `v0.38.4` and vendored it back, and updated the PR. PTAL again, thanks again for catching this.

This looks far more reasonable, thanks for the quick turnaround.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/96549 should go in first, since it is a targeted dep update of x/net and x/sys to address the http/2 bug, then this will need a rebase (and won't need to bump x/net and x/sys, since that PR includes versions as new or newer than what is included in this PR).

/lgtm
/approve
/hold for https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/96549

issue_context.body: For each kubernetes release, we need to cut a new cadvisor release and vendor it back into k/k. This issue will track cutting new cadvisor release (v0.38.0) and vendoring it back into k/k for 1.20 release.

@bobbypage let's make sure we have a good sync of dependencies between containerd<>runc<>cadvisor<>kubernetes<>docker/docker - basically check if all of them are the same or similar enough for us to use newest deps in k/k.

Thanks @dims.

I took a look and tried to upgrade cadvisor to latest master as a test and it looks like the following dependencies will need to be updated in k/k as part of the upgrade:

Taken from
```
$ hack/pin-dependency.sh github.com/google/cadvisor master
$ hack/update-vendor.sh
$ hack/lint-dependencies.sh
```

    hack/pin-dependency.sh github.com/docker/docker v17.12.0-ce-rc1.0.20200916142827-bd33bbf0497b+incompatible

so looks like in addition the updates mentioned in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/96287#issuecomment-723283985 `github.com/checkpoint-restore/go-criu/v4` and `github.com/opencontainers/selinux` need to be updated.

New cadvisor release (v0.38.0) has been cut -- https://github.com/google/cadvisor/releases/tag/v0.38.0

Next step will be to vendor it back into k/k
